sources.title: E-visa to Belarus
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus
sources.officialityEvidence: Belarus MFA’s live page names the limited ordinary-passport eVisa cohort and its process, but does not identify Kosovo.

sources.title: Visa regime of the Republic of Kazakhstan for foreign citizens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan
sources.officialityEvidence: Kazakhstan MFA’s live government table separates diplomatic, service and ordinary passport regimes but does not identify Kosovo.

sources.title: How to get an e-visa?
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live central-government procedure makes nationality-list inclusion a condition of electronic issuance; it provides no Kosovo result.
sources.supportingExcerpt: country of citizenship is included in the list of countries whose citizens are eligible to receive an e-visa

sources.title: List of countries eligible for Mongolian E-Visa

sources.title: Countries Not Requiring a Visa

unresolved.reason: The Azerbaijani MFA visa-regime host fails normal TLS validation. No accessible current Azerbaijani or Kosovo authority directly maps an ordinary Kosovo passport to a visitor route or issuance timing.

Belarus MFA’s named ordinary-passport eVisa cohort does not identify Kosovo. No current Belarusian or Kosovo authority directly maps its ordinary passport to an advance, electronic, arrival or exempt route.

No current accessible Gabonese or Kosovo authority directly maps an ordinary Kosovo passport to a visitor route or issuance timing. eVisa availability or passport recognition is not treated as eligibility.

No current accessible Equatorial Guinean or Kosovo authority directly maps an ordinary Kosovo passport to a visitor route or issuance timing. Generic electronic-visa workflows do not resolve nationality eligibility.
Kazakhstan’s current passport-type table and eVisa procedure do not identify Kosovo. The absence of a row cannot establish a visa-required, electronic or arrival route.
Mongolia’s current named tourist-waiver and eVisa rosters do not identify Kosovo. Neither makes an unlisted-passport consequence explicit, so no route is inferred.
Montserrat’s current required and not-required lists both omit Kosovo. No territory or Kosovo authority directly supplies a Kosovo ordinary-passport route; their omission is not a complement.
No current Russian or Kosovo authority directly establishes that an ordinary Kosovo passport is recognized for a nationwide short-visitor route or identifies its issuance timing.

No current Serbian or Kosovo authority directly establishes a nationwide ordinary Kosovo-passport visitor route or issuance timing. Recognition and Serbian country-register omission are not visa rules.
Uzbekistan MFA’s current visa-free and electronic-visa schedules do not identify Kosovo. Its generic procedure does not establish a Kosovo-specific recognized passport or issuance route.
